```yaml
name: Nuitka Linux Build

on:
  push:
    branches: [ "master", "main" ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ "master", "main" ]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build-linux:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.9", "3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python ${{ matrix.python-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install nuitka
          # Install dirsearch dependencies if required for compilation context
          pip install -r requirements.txt || true

      - name: Compile with Nuitka
        run: |
          nuitka \
            --standalone \
            --onefile \
            --output-dir=dist \
            --output-filename=dirsearch \
            --include-package=dirsearch \
            dirsearch.py

      - name: Handle Nuitka output name differences
        run: |
          # Nuitka on Linux typically produces a binary named after the script.
          # However, depending on the version or flags, it might vary slightly.
          # We ensure the binary exists and is executable.
          
          DIST_DIR="dist"
          EXPECTED_BINARY="dirsearch"
          
          if [ -f "$DIST_DIR/$EXPECTED_BINARY" ]; then
            echo "Found expected binary: $DIST_DIR/$EXPECTED_BINARY"
            chmod +x "$DIST_DIR/$EXPECTED_BINARY"
          else
            echo "Expected binary not found. Searching for alternatives..."
            # List files in dist to debug
            ls -la "$DIST_DIR"
            
            # Try to find any executable file in the dist directory
            FOUND_BINARY=$(find "$DIST_DIR" -type f -executable -name "dirsearch*" | head -n 1)
            
            if [ -n "$FOUND_BINARY" ]; then
              echo "Found alternative binary: $FOUND_BINARY"
              # Move or copy to expected name for consistency in subsequent steps
              cp "$FOUND_BINARY" "$DIST_DIR/$EXPECTED_BINARY"
              chmod +x "$DIST_DIR/$EXPECTED_BINARY"
            else
              echo "Error: No suitable binary found in $DIST_DIR"
              exit 1
            fi
          fi

      - name: Test compiled binary
        run: |
          ./dist/dirsearch --help

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: dirsearch-linux-py${{ matrix.python-version }}
          path: dist/dirsearch
          retention-days: 5
```
